question.text: Under Solon, all Athenian citizens were allowed to participate in the ekklesia assembly that met in a building southwest of this elevated part of the city, which is home to the Parthenon.
question.clue: This site of the Propylaea also featured six women taking the place of columns on its Caryatid Porch.

swap.leadin: After this battle, Pheidippides ran approximately 26 miles to Athens to announce a Greek victory.
swap.text: Name this 490 BCE battle that lends its name to a very long race.
swap.clue: Prior to this battle, forces led by Datis and Artaphernes ("ar-ta-FER-neez") stood at odds for eight days against Miltiades's ("milt-EYE-ad-eezʼs") army.

question.leadin: Answer the following about historians of the ancient world.
question.text: Despite telling tales of giant ants and massive armies, this Greek is known as the "Father of Histories" for his work the Histories, which details the Persian Wars in addition to providing interesting if not accurate ethnographies of various classical peoples.
question.clue: This author likely confused marmots for giant gold-digging ants in India.

swap.leadin: Name these Wonders of the Ancient World.
swap.text: This tall bronze statue on the island of Rhodes was not, in fact, tall enough to span the harbor, but few people could link their arms around one of its thumbs.
swap.clue: An Egyptian offer to rebuild this structure was refused after a 226 BCE earthquake destroyed it.

question.text: Multiple members of the Annales school, wrote their theses about this Spanish king's influence on politics in the Mediterranean. He sent the warships that won the Battle of Lepanto.
question.answerHtml: Philip II [“the second”] [accept Felipe II; prompt on Philip and Felipe]
question.clue: During his reign, an Ottoman fleet commanded by Sufi Ali Pasha was defeated by this king's half-brother John of Austria in the Battle of Lepanto.

swap.text: The First Punic War broke out after the Romans allied with this city to attack the Carthaginian base at Akragas. At the Battle of Himera, a king of this city named Gelon defeated Hamilcar I.
swap.clue: The Spartan general Gyllipus defended this city from Athenians under Nicias during an expedition in the Peloponnesian War, and it was originally a Corinthian colony.

question.leadin: Answer the following about numerically-named groups in ancient Greece.
question.text: This Greek historian chronicled the fighting retreat of the Ten Thousand, a Greek mercenary army in Persia, in his Anabasis. This student of Socrates also wrote a biography of Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: Another of his works attributes qualities of an ideal ruler to the conqueror of Astyages and the Medes, and is one of the most important Greek examples of the "mirror for princes" genre.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Battle of Leuctra.
swap.text: The Battle of Leuctra unusually saw this fighting force placed on the left side of the army while they were commanded by Epaminondas. This force would later be annihilated by Phillip II at the Battle of Chaeronea.
swap.clue: This group played a major role in winning a decisive victory at the Battle of Leuctra.

question.leadin: Their name meant "successors" and they included Antipater, Perdiccas, and Craterus.
question.text: Give the Greek term for these generals and administrators who scrambled to increase their personal power after the death of Alexander.
question.clue: Conflict between these people began when their former leader granted his kingdom "to the strongest."

swap.text: The congregation of the Archbishop of Candia--modern day Irakloion--were massacred here during the Greek War of Independence. Some artifacts here are written in the Linear A script.
swap.clue: Modern archaeologists no longer agree that a civilization on this island collapsed after an eruption of Thera.

question.leadin: Legendarily during this battle, a female apparition chastised a navy for backing their ships away.
question.text: Name this September 480 B.C. naval battle fought near the namesake straits, which was won by Greek forces under Themistocles. It is considered one of the pivotal battles in the Greco-Persian War.
question.clue: The victors at this battle had earlier suffered a defeat at Artemisium, and following this battle, the losers suffered a defeat at Mychale and another at Plataea.

swap.leadin: A gold funerary mask found at this site was dubbed the "Mask of Agamemnon" by Heinrich Schliemann.
swap.text: Name this archeological site. It names a phase of the Greek bronze age which followed the Minoan civilization and was likely destroyed by the Dorian invasion.
swap.clue: This culture originated the title potnia given to its great mother goddess, constructed huge beehive-shaped tombs called tholoi, and used the Linear B writing system.

question.leadin: This man legendarily promulgated an oral constitution that established the Gerousia, a council of 28 elders.
question.text: Name this lawgiver whose Rhetra also included a dual monarchy for Sparta.
question.clue: This legendary lawgiver who established the Great Rhetra constitution, outlined the function of the five ephors, and called for a council of twenty-eight men known as the gerousia to wield equal power to the two royal houses.

swap.text: This Spartan king, a descendant of Eurysthenes, underwent the agoge system and fought at the Battle of Sepeia. He later led Greek forces at the Battle of Thermopylae, which saw the heroics of 300 Spartans.
swap.clue: Ephialtes betrayed this husband of Queen Gorgo by identifying a path around his forces.

question.leadin: This script was likely used concurrently with Cretan hieroglyphs, whose standard Archanes ("ar-KAY-nees") Formula has been compared to this script's "libation formula"
question.text: Name this writing system used in the middle Minoan period. Many tablets inscribed with this script have been found at the Hagia Triada site.
question.clue: This script used by the Minoan civilization is one of the two undeciphered ancient Greek scripts along with Cretan Hieroglyphs. It is believed to be the origin of a similarly named script used by the later Mycenaeans.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the economic history of the successor rump states that emerged from the 1204 Sack of Constantinople.
swap.text: It's not the Morea, but religious silver coins were produced by the mint at Arta that operated under the "Despotate" of this ancient region of western Greece and Albania. Home to the oracle at Dodona, this region's Molossians were led by a king who defeated Rome at Heraclea and Asculum.
swap.clue: That king of this region ignored his advisor Cineas and came to the aid of Tarentum, leading to a defeat at Beneventum.

question.text: Troops from this city were the only ones to help Athens at the Battle of Marathon. According to Herodotus, Aristides ("air-ih-STY-deez") the Just led Athenian forces at a battle near this city that was honored with the "Serpent Column."
question.clue: This city's strategic position came from its overlooking the road from Thebes to Corinth.

swap.text: Modern scholars use this term to describe the first stage of the Peloponnesian War, named for one of the Spartan kings who developed the strategy of intermittently ravaging the farmland of Attica.

question.leadin: In this passage an invading army dismisses their weaker opponents' expression of hope in the gods with the dictum that "The strong do what they can; the weak suffer what they must."
question.text: Name this important passage for the Realist School of International Relations, a section of the History of the Peloponnesian War.
question.clue: A party in this passage notes that "the Cretan Sea is a wide one" to explain how a man such as Brasidas could evade a blockade.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Leonidas' predecessor Cleomenes I.
swap.text: Cleomenes I waged war against this other city and defeated it at the Battle of Sepeia in 494 BC. This city earlier defeated Sparta at Hysiae, during which it was ruled by Pheidon.
swap.clue: This city's Hybristica ("hye-BRIS-tick-uh") festival has been linked to its supposed defence after the Battle of Sepeia ("SEH-pay-ah") by the female poet Telesilla.
